text:
The NFL's Week 10 slate delivered plenty of drama. However, several teams left the weekend worrying about something far more important than the final score. Multiple high-profile players suffered potentially significant injuries. Those include franchise quarterbacks, elite pass-catchers, and defensive stars. The most alarming developments came in Munich, where Drake Maye and Aidan Hutchinson were hurt on the same play. Brock Bowers also avoided what initially looked like a devastating ankle injury. Meanwhile, Geno Smith, Drake London and others face uncertain timelines. Here is a closer look at the biggest NFL Week 10 injury developments.

QB Drake Maye, New England Patriots

Patriots fans were left holding their breath during Sunday's 35-10 international loss to the Detroit Lions in Munich. Maye injured his right ankle after being brought down by Hutchinson on an opening-drive sack and did not return. New England reportedly fears the quarterback may have suffered an ankle fracture that could end his season. Further evaluation is necessary before a definitive diagnosis or recovery timeline can be established.

The Patriots enter their Week 11 bye at 5-5, giving the organization additional time to assess its options. If Maye is sidelined, Tommy DeVito is the quarterback who finished Sunday's game and would be the leading candidate to take over. Wide receiver SJ Brown also aggravated a hamstring injury against Detroit, adding another concern to New England's offense.

DE Aidan Hutchinson, Detroit Lions

Detroit's dominant victory came at a devastating cost. Hutchinson suffered a torn right ACL while celebrating a third-down sack of Maye. Hutchinson is expected to miss the remainder of the season. Further testing is also being conducted to determine whether additional knee damage occurred.

Losing Hutchinson is an enormous blow to the Lions defense. He recorded his sixth sack of the season before going down. Kelvin Sheppard will now have to find new ways to generate consistent pressure.

TE Brock Bowers, Las Vegas Raiders

Bowers' ankle injury was another major concern after the Raiders' 21-13 home loss to Seattle. The star tight end was hurt during the opening drive. He briefly returned after receiving treatment. However, he eventually left the contest for good. Fortunately, Monday brought encouraging news. Head coach Klint Kubiak said it was not as bad as initially feared. They have listed Bowers as day-to-day while further evaluations continue.

That is a major relief for Las Vegas. Bowers leads the Raiders in receiving and remains a central piece of the passing attack. Any absence would place additional pressure on Michael Mayer and the team's other receiving options, particularly with the offense trying to develop consistency.

QB Geno Smith, New York Jets

The Jets' frustrating 2026 campaign took another hit during Sunday's 31-12 loss to Buffalo. Smith initially underwent a concussion evaluation after taking a hit. He did clear the assessment and return to the game. Unfortunately, he subsequently suffered an ankle injury and was ruled out.

Smith avoided leaving the stadium in a walking boot. Still, that alone does not establish the severity of the injury. Further evaluation will determine whether he can return for Week 11. With New York sitting at 2-8, the coaching staff has little reason to rush its starting quarterback back prematurely. Cade Klubnik stepped in after Smith exited. Wide receiver Omar Cooper Jr. also aggravated an ankle injury and did not return.

WR Drake London, Atlanta Falcons

Atlanta's 35-13 loss to Kansas City also came with a worrying development. London sustained a possible concussion. He was evaluated during the contest. His availability will depend on the results of further assessments and whether he enters or progresses through the NFL's concussion protocol.

At 3-7, the Falcons can ill afford to lose their leading perimeter threat. If London cannot return promptly, Atlanta will need Kyle Pitts Sr. and its remaining receivers to shoulder more of the passing-game responsibility.

RB Woody Marks, Houston Texans

Houston's backfield situation also deserves attention after Sunday's 27-24 loss to Cleveland. Marks exited with a knee injury, not a concussion as initially reported. The Texans' official Week 10 injury report listed him with a knee issue. He had been able to participate in practice before the game.

With Houston scheduled for Thursday night football in Week 11, the short turnaround makes his availability worth monitoring. David Montgomery and the team's other backfield options could be asked to shoulder additional work if Marks cannot go.

WR Jordan Addison, Minnesota Vikings

Addison missed Minnesota's 30-10 divisional victory over Green Bay after injuring his thumb during Friday's practice. He was ruled out for the matchup. His return will depend on how the injury responds and whether he can safely catch passes.

Justin Jefferson and the Vikings' remaining receiving options handled the workload against Green Bay. Of course, getting Addison back would give the passing attack another important dimension.

Other notable Week 10 injuries

Several other teams are monitoring important players. Pittsburgh guard Mason McCormick suffered an ankle injury, while safety DeShon Elliott was ruled out with a knee issue. Kansas City guard Trey Smith exited with a concussion. Seattle lost running back George Holani (knee) and right tackle Abraham Lucas (ankle). Indianapolis tackle Bernhard Raimann was ruled out after a concussion evaluation. Cincinnati guard Dalton Risner was listed with an illness rather than a knee injury.

Derrick Moore and DJ Wonnum are capable vets and will fill in, but they’re nowhere near Hutchinson’s level.

The Lions won on Sunday without Hutchinson for most of the game to improve to 7-2, and perhaps they have enough wins banked to make the playoffs in what will be a difficult wild-card race. But their hopes of being a Super Bowl contender are likely dashed without their two best defensive players.

title: Mason McCormick's injury will test Steelers' biggest strength: Their offensive line - NFL.com
description:
Pittsburgh built an identity and rode a four-game winning streak heading into Sunday night thanks in large part to their young and developing offensive line.

text:
The medical staff rushed onto the field Sunday in Cincinnati as Mason McCormick writhed in pain on the turf. The severity of the injury and the way the Pittsburgh Steelers' feel about their starting left guard were clear from the player's reaction. As the doctors and trainers fastened an air cast to McCormick's right ankle and prepared to cart him off the field, teammates gathered around on a knee. Emotions flowed.

"It made a lot of us sick to our stomach," tackle Troy Fautanu said. "I've never seen anything like that before."

During the 38-18 blowout, the Bengals exposed the weaknesses on the Steelers' roster, particularly Pittsburgh's defensive backs and injury-marred receiving corps. As the Steelers look to move past the letdown, they will now be challenged to maintain their strength in the trenches without a key cog.

Pittsburgh built an identity and rode a four-game winning streak heading into Sunday night thanks in large part to their young and developing offensive line. From Weeks 5 through 8, only one team accumulated more rushing yards than Pittsburgh's 564, and only two had a better yard per carry average than the Steelers' 5.3. At a position group in which continuity and chemistry are critical, the Steelers' offensive line will be tested to maintain that high level of play without one of the players most responsible for its success.

"It's definitely a time to rally around it, because that was definitely a dynamic of this football team that we all want, especially me," Steelers coach Mike McCarthy said. "I believe it starts in the trenches. I think the tradition, the history of the Steelers reflects that.

"We'll continue to go down that road, but it's time for others to step up. This is how every season goes. Unfortunately, you have injuries, and it's opportunity for others. But it's also an opportunity for us to make sure we're utilizing all of our resources."

The Steelers' most significant investments up front may have come at tackle, with a pair of first-round picks in Fautanu and Max Iheanachor, and at center with second-round selection Zach Frazier. But the personality of the offensive line and the heartbeat flowed through the two trash-talking guards. Thrust into a starting role in the middle of his rookie season, McCormick has consistently improved to become a mauling run blocker, reliable pass protector and excellent communicator.

"I'll just tell you from my perspective, Mason is clearly one of the leaders on the team," McCarthy said, adding that McCormick is on the team's leadership council.

Fautanu has often said there's no one else he'd rather play alongside. Now, he has no choice in the matter. On Monday, McCarthy acknowledged that McCormick sustained a significant injury but did not have a definitive timeline. If the Steelers are going to maintain their playoff position and make some noise in December and January, they'll need to weather this injury.

Versatile lineman Spencer Anderson appears to be the next man up. Drafted in the seventh round in 2023, Anderson has exceeded his draft position and proven to be a malleable piece of the offensive line. Over the years, he's contributed at tackle, guard and as the sixth offensive lineman in jumbo packages.

"Spencer's just a 360 football player in my view," McCarthy said. "Just coming in here to see to see him play in different positions… He's a gifted football player. This will be his opportunity."

Where the starting left guard position goes from here will hinge upon a number of factors, including McCormick's recovery timeline, Anderson's performance and the readiness of rookie third-round pick Gennings Dunker, who is one of the x-factors.

At the University of Iowa, Dunker was arguably the most consistent lineman from a group that won the Joe Moore Award as the top offensive line in college football. The Hawkeyes' run-heavy style of play was reflected in Dunker's performance early in camp. His tape told two stories. As a run blocker, Dunker is already an old-school mauler, using his tree-trunk legs to punish defenders. However, he still needed considerable refinement as a pass protector, especially as he makes the transition from college tackle to NFL guard. McCarthy said that Dunker is "definitely part of the conversation" as the Steelers consider different possibilities.

Whether it's Anderson, Dunker or some combination of the two, the Steelers will need to continue to lean on the men up front, even with one of the most important pieces missing. How well they handle the injury will play a major role in determing where the season goes from here.

If Mayfield is unable to play on Sunday in Detroit, rookie quarterback Jalon Daniels would draw his fourth start of the season with Stick serving as his backup.

Stick was previously active for each of Daniels' three starts in Weeks 4-6 as Mayfield was recovering from a dislocated right thumb. In each of those three weeks, however, he was elevated from the practice squad to be eligible for the game, and that is the maximum number of practice squad elevations per player during the regular season.

Stick was signed to the Buccaneers' practice squad on August 31 but he has prior experience in Offensive Coordinator Zac Robinson's system, as the two were together last season with the Atlanta Falcons. A fifth-round pick by the Los Angeles Chargers in 2019, Stick has appeared in a total of six games with four starts, completing 111 of 174 passes (63.8%) for 1,129 yards, three touchdowns, one interception and an 85.7 passer rating.

Rush also has NFL starting experience, having opened 18 games with Dallas, Baltimore and Atlanta. That includes two starts for the Falcons this season, as he joined Atlanta near the end of July and started the first two games of the regular season before being released on October 19. In all, Rush has played in 44 games and has completed 386 of 635 passes (60.8%) for 3,995 yards, 21 touchdowns and 18 interceptions. His most extensive playing time came with the Cowboys in 2024, when he started eight games and compiled a 4-4 record while throwing 12 touchdown passes against five interceptions. Rush initially entered the NFL as an undrafted free agent out of Central Michigan with the Cowboys in 2017.

Sills was on the Buccaneers' active roster for three weeks before being waived on November 10, which created the roster spot now used for Stick's promotion. He started the season on injured reserve but was activated on October 22 and played in three games, though without drawing a target in the pass game. Tampa Bay signed Sills as a free agent in April, also reuniting him with Robinson, who had also been his coordinator in Atlanta in 2025 when he put up a career-best 18 catches for 191 yards and two touchdowns. He has also played for the New York Giants and Denver Broncos, and in 33 career games (11 starts), he has recorded 31 receptions for 314 yards and two scores.

Johnson was on the Buccaneers' practice squad for five weeks. He previously saw regular season action with the Philadelphia Eagles in 2025, appearing three games with one start.

title: Aidan Hutchinson Is To Blame For Freak Injury, Must Tone Down Celebrations
description:
The Detroit Lions continued their winning ways Sunday morning in Munich, Germany, easily defeating the New England Patriots, 35-10, for their fifth straight win.
Yet, the Week 10 victory was overshadowed by the likely season-ending knee injury to EDGE Aidan Hutchinson, the Lions’ star pass-rusher.
His sack of Maye was his seventh on the season, and he also logged another two pressures in the international affair, bringing his season total to 52 (the second-highest total in the NFL).
I'm fully aware that players like Hutchinson are also entertainers and that they have a genuine passion and love for playing the game.
He needs to be steadfast with it and emphasize there is no wiggle room for a Hutchinson 2.0.
text:
The Detroit Lions continued their winning ways Sunday morning in Munich, Germany, easily defeating the New England Patriots, 35-10, for their fifth straight win.

It was a dominant effort from start to finish for Dan Campbell's team, which accumulated nearly 500 total yards (494) and allowed just 151 yards to Mike Vrabel's squad.

Yet, the Week 10 victory was overshadowed by the likely season-ending knee injury to EDGE Aidan Hutchinson, the Lions’ star pass-rusher.

Hutchinson suffered the injury while celebrating a first-quarter sack of Patriots signal-caller Drake Maye; he leaped in the air and upon coming down, landed awkwardly on his right leg. The fifth-year defender never played another snap Sunday.

If that was not a clear-cut sign to cut the acrobatics out of his celebration repertoire, I don't know what would be. Nonetheless, he needs to – no ifs, ands, or buts about it.

The University of Michigan product will receive further testing upon returning home to the states. However, his 2026 campaign is believed to be over, cutting short what had been an All-Pro-caliber season.

His sack of Maye was his seventh on the season, and he also logged another two pressures in the international affair, bringing his season total to 52 (the second-highest total in the NFL).

He easily was one of the league's most productive pass-rushers in 2026, earning a league-leading Pro Football Focus pass-rush grade of 91.1 and an overall mark of 91.9 through nine games (the best overall grade among 111 qualified EDGEs).

Plain and simple, Detroit does not possess another EDGE defender in the same stratosphere as the 2022 No. 2 overall pick. Derrick Moore and DJ Wonnum have each had their moments of looking like competent pass-rushers. However, neither of them is going to be confused for Hutchinson anytime soon.

The Michigan native has become an irreplaceable talent; consequently, losing him for the year is undoubtedly a detrimental blow to Lions defensive coordinator Kelvin Sheppard's unit. Without the premier quarterback disruptor, it certainly is harder to envision Detroit capturing the NFC North crown and making a Super Bowl run.

It begs the question: Should Lions head man Dan Campbell mandate that his players are no longer allowed to leave their feet to celebrate big plays? If I were Campbell, I would do just that.

And no, I'm not trying to take the fun out of the game. I'm fully aware that players like Hutchinson are also entertainers and that they have a genuine passion and love for playing the game. So, I would never want to take away their ability to enjoy themselves while they put their bodies on the line 17 weeks a year. That would be a bad look for Campbell, too, and likely cause him to lose the respect of his players.

It's why the celebrations can and should remain. However, they need to be toned down. And specifically, I'm talking about eliminating the acrobatics, and in the process, reducing the likelihood of another Lions player suffering a season-ending ailment while celebrating a major play.

And Campbell can't sugarcoat the importance of this being the new celebration policy, either. He needs to be steadfast with it and emphasize there is no wiggle room for a Hutchinson 2.0. The NFC North is too good and deep, with the Bears continuing to rack up wins and Kirk Cousins now under center for the Vikings, for the Lions to endure another celebration gone wrong.

text:
The Buffalo Bills are running through opposing quarterback depth charts almost as quickly as they're running through opponents.

Kyle McCord is next.

Buffalo will face its sixth backup quarterback in four games when the former Syracuse star makes his second career start for the Miami Dolphins on Sunday at Highmark Stadium.

It will mark the third straight week the Bills have faced a quarterback who had never thrown an NFL regular-season pass before November.

The Bills (8-1) have won five straight games and allowed just one touchdown over their last three. Their defensive resurgence has coincided with a rash of injuries to opposing quarterbacks, some of which Buffalo has inflicted.

Miami placed starting quarterback Malik Willis on injured reserve last week with a groin injury, opening the door for McCord to make his NFL debut against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday.

Bills defense has feasted on backup quarterbacks

The revolving door began Nov. 1 when Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson injured his throwing thumb on the first offensive snap of the game.

Backup Tyler Huntley suffered a toe injury in the second quarter, thrusting undrafted rookie Joe Fagnano into his first NFL game.

Minnesota Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray missed the following week's game with a hamstring injury. Carson Wentz started and posted an 8.9 passer rating before being replaced by Max Brosmer in the fourth quarter.

New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith exited twice against Buffalo on Sunday, first to be evaluated for a concussion and then with an ankle injury. Fourth-round rookie Cade Klubnik made his NFL debut in relief.

Here's how the five backup quarterbacks have fared against Buffalo:

Tyler Huntley, Ravens: 2-for-4, 0 yards

Joe Fagnano, Ravens: 10-for-21, 91 yards, INT

Carson Wentz, Vikings: 8-for-25, 81 yards, 2 INTs

Max Brosmer, Vikings: 6-for-7, 58 yards

Cade Klubnik, Jets: 11-for-20, 137 yards, INT

That's a combined 48.1% completion percentage, 367 passing yards, zero touchdowns, four interceptions and a 41.4 passer rating.

Buffalo has outscored its opponents 90-28 during that stretch.

Kyle McCord sets Dolphins record in NFL debut

McCord made franchise history in his first NFL game despite Miami's 24-22 loss to the Colts on Sunday.

He completed 17 of 32 passes for 209 yards, the most passing yards by a Dolphins quarterback in his NFL debut.

McCord didn't throw a touchdown pass or an interception but ran for a touchdown and lost a fumble in his own end zone that Indianapolis recovered for a touchdown.

Miami nearly overcame a 21-7 second-half deficit despite kicker Zane Gonzalez missing two field goals and an extra point.

Dolphins coach Jeff Hafley was encouraged by McCord's demeanor.

“He was composed, he didn't get rattled,” Hafley said.

McCord, 24, spent three seasons at Ohio State before transferring to Syracuse, where he put together one of the most prolific passing seasons in ACC history.

He led the nation with 4,779 passing yards in 2024, setting an ACC single-season record, and threw 34 touchdown passes while leading the Orange to a 10-3 record.

The Philadelphia Eagles selected McCord in the sixth round of the 2025 NFL Draft and he spent his rookie season on their practice squad.

He signed with the Green Bay Packers in January and completed 46 of 70 passes for 446 yards, four touchdowns and no interceptions in three preseason games. Green Bay traded him to Miami for a 2028 sixth-round draft pick in August.

His second career start will bring him back to upstate New York to face a defense that hasn't surrendered a touchdown since the first quarter of November.

text:
Detroit Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson will miss the rest of the NFL season after sustaining a serious knee injury while celebrating.

Hutchinson, 26, jumped in the air after bringing down New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye in the first quarter of the Lions' 35-10 win in Munich.

The 2022 second overall pick fell to the ground shortly after landing, clutching his right knee.

Hutchinson walked to the sideline after medical treatment on the field but did not return to the game - and has torn his anterior cruciate ligament.

It is the second season-ending injury of Hutchinson career - but Lions head coach Dan Campbell has no plans to stop his players from expressing themselves.

"I hate it. I think we all understand what it is, and let's be smart, but no, I'm not gonna say 'nobody celebrates any more'," Campbell said.

"The number of moves that I've seen 'Hutch' make and the number of plyometrics, explosive movements, the spins, the one-leg lateral movements, lateral balances... it was one of those things, man."

This was the sixth regular-season NFL game to be played in Germany and the third to be held at Bayern Munich's Allianz Arena.

The Lions' win means they are top of the NFC North and have the second-best record in the conference.

Hutchinson is regarded as one of the premier pass rushers in the NFL, and is currently tied for 13th in the league with six sacks this season.

Campbell is confident Hutchinson will come back stronger on his return from the injury setback.

"He's such a phenomenal player, an impact player, but more importantly he's an unbelievable team-mate and he's one of our captains," Campbell added.

"What a hell of a year he was having. He's just improved every year and to come off the injury he had [in 2024].

"This guy will overcome this and he will come back better than he was. It's just the way he is, it's the way he's wired."

text:
Tyreek Hill is leaving no stone unturned in his attempt to return to the NFL. Nearly 14 months after suffering a serious knee injury, the free-agent wide receiver is still working to regain the strength and explosiveness that made him one of football's most dangerous playmakers. His latest step has taken him overseas, where he has turned to a physician who has worked with some of the biggest names in international sport, including Usain Bolt.

Hill recently shared a social-media update revealing that he has travelled overseas to work with a doctor who had helped several sporting greats.

"Went overseas to work with the Doc who's helped some of the GOATs. The comeback continues. ????????" Hill wrote on X.

He posted a video with it, which showed Hill in Munich, Germany. In the clip, renowned sports physician Dr. Hans-Wilhelm Müller-Wohlfahrt could be seen working on Hill's injured knee.

Tyreek Hill's pursuit of elite medical expertise signals serious intent for his return. Subscribe to stay updated on how this unconventional approach reshapes his comeback timeline.

Müller-Wohlfahrt is no stranger to elite athletes. He spent more than four decades as Bayern Munich's team doctor and also worked with the German national football team from 1995 to 2018. His patients have included Jamaican sprint legend Usain Bolt, whose connection with the physician makes Hill's decision particularly interesting.

In a 2018 interview with BILD, Müller-Wohlfahrt discussed treating Bolt before the 2016 Rio Olympics. The Jamaican went on to win gold in the 100 meters, 200 meters, and 4×100-meter relay at those Games. For Hill, working with a doctor who has treated an athlete of Bolt's stature could be another important step in his recovery.

Hill's need for that help stems from the devastating injury he suffered on September 29, 2025. Playing for the Miami Dolphins against the New York Jets, he dislocated his left knee and sustained multiple ligament tears, including an ACL injury. The setback ended his season and required two operations. Miami eventually released him on February 16, 2026, after he failed a physical.

The road back has not been easy. In July, Hill spoke about the challenge of rebuilding strength in his injured leg and described his rehabilitation as a day-by-day process. His trip to Munich is another part of that effort, although there is no confirmation that the treatment has resulted in medical clearance.

The latest update on his return prospects came from his agent, Drew Rosenhaus. Appearing on The Pat McAfee Show on November 10, Rosenhaus confirmed that Hill had not yet been medically cleared but suggested that the receiver was getting close.

"As soon as Tyreek Hill is healthy and cleared medically, I'm letting teams know they can sign him. I think he's close, and I think he's gonna make a great comeback. I expect him to be playing and making things happen this season," Rosenhaus said.

Rosenhaus also indicated that Hill could receive clearance within the next few weeks. That remains an expectation rather than a confirmed timeline. Until doctors give him the green light, the wide receiver will have to wait for his next NFL opportunity.

The Kansas City Chiefs are among the teams linked with a possible move. In October, NBC Sports reported, citing The Athletic's Mike Silver, that the Chiefs were "very interested" in bringing Hill back and had contacted Rosenhaus. The report quickly sparked talk of a reunion with the franchise where Hill spent the first six seasons of his NFL career.

Hill won Super Bowl LIV with Kansas City and became one of Patrick Mahomes' most dangerous offensive weapons. The Chiefs traded him to Miami in March 2022, but a return has remained a talking point since his release. Still, the October report does not confirm that Kansas City made an offer or that a deal is close. Hill's medical clearance remains the biggest hurdle.

There is also a legal matter surrounding the receiver. On October 13, a Miami jury found Hill liable for two battery claims brought by his estranged wife, Lakeeta Vaccaro, and awarded her $500,000 in compensatory damages. The jury found Hill not liable on eight other claims. During the trial, Hill denied most of the allegations, describing them as false, although he acknowledged shoving Vaccaro in one incident. Following the verdict, the NFL said the matter remained under review under its personal conduct policy.

For now, Hill has one priority: getting healthy enough to play again. Rosenhaus believes the receiver is nearing that point, but the final decision rests with the medical professionals evaluating his knee. Until he receives clearance, a return to Kansas City or any other NFL team remains a possibility, not a done deal.

text:
Jets quarterback Geno Smith went for tests on his injured ankle on Monday, but it doesn’t look like they turned up anything that will keep him from playing against the Chargers in Week 11.

Ian Rapoport of NFL Media reports that tests showed Smith avoided a major injury during the 31-12 loss to the Bills on Sunday. Smith left the game in the third quarter and rookie Cade Klubnik ran the offense the rest of the way.

Smith also went for a concussion evaluation during the loss, but head coach Aaron Glenn said on Monday that Smith will start this week as long as he is cleared medically.

Smith has started every game for the Jets this season. He has completed 67.1 percent of his passes for 2,226 yards, 12 touchdowns and three interceptions, but the Jets rank 26th in the league with 19.4 points per game.

title: Aidan Hutchinson injury update: Detroit Lions DE has torn ACL; 'no other significant damage'
description:

Unfortunately, those fears were confirmed back in Michigan, as Hutchinson tore his ACL and will miss the rest of the Lions’ 2026 season, according to NFL Insider Tom Pelissero.
Still, it’s a huge blow to the Lions’ 2026 season, considering Hutchinson was the most disruptive force on the team’s defense.
Through 11 games, Hutchinson had amassed 6.0 sacks, one forced fumble, and 52 pressures (trailing only Buffalo EDGE Greg Rousseau).
Hutchinson has only been responsible for 6.0 of the team’s 32 sacks (he had 14.5 of the team’s 49 last year).
text:
On Sunday, reports emerged that Detroit Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson was feared to have suffered a season-ending knee injury, but the team would continue to do more tests when they arrived back in the United States. Unfortunately, those fears were confirmed back in Michigan, as Hutchinson tore his ACL and will miss the rest of the Lions’ 2026 season, according to NFL Insider Tom Pelissero.

If there is any positive news to glean from this situation, it is that additional testing revealed no further knee damage, which was also a major concern immediately after the injury.

Still, it’s a huge blow to the Lions’ 2026 season, considering Hutchinson was the most disruptive force on the team’s defense. Through 11 games, Hutchinson had amassed 6.0 sacks, one forced fumble, and 52 pressures (trailing only Buffalo EDGE Greg Rousseau). More than that, he was a force multiplier, making his teammates around him better by drawing more attention and bodies away from them.

On Sunday night after the Lions’ win over the New England Patriots, coach Dan Campbell noted they’ll need several players to step up if Hutchinson’s absence lasts.

“We gotta go. We’ll see where Hutch is at, but we’ve gotta step up now,” Campbell said. “We need some guys to really step up—and if that is the case (with a serious Hutchinson injury), fill that role.”

Detroit has been able to put together more of a diverse pass rush this year. Hutchinson has only been responsible for 6.0 of the team’s 32 sacks (he had 14.5 of the team’s 49 last year). The Lions have gotten a fair amount of production from Alim McNeill (6.5 sacks), DJ Wonnum (6.0), Derrick Moore (4.0), and Skyler Gill-Howard (2.0) along their defensive front.

“We like ‘em. That’s why we acquired them when we did,” Campbell said of their remaining defensive linemen. “And I know this: Derrick Moore gets better every game. The more reps he gets, he gets better. It was good to get Wonnum back today. We know what Mac [McNeill] is, Sky. So can Tyleik (Williams). And all those guys, even Levi (Onwuzurike), (Tyler) Lacy, they play a different flavor, but they push the pocket; they got movement. But I think the important thing is, man, we knew we had to do to get out of this game with a win. We had to play really good defense.”

For Hutchinson, it’s a devastating blow to his career. Just two years ago, he suffered a gruesome broken leg that ended his 2024 season. And while he returned to full health and form in both 2025 and 2026, recovering from a torn ACL brings a whole new set of challenges for Hutchinson.

text:
FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith, who underwent imaging tests Monday on his left ankle, avoided a major injury, sources told the NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

Smith dealt with a variety of injuries during Sunday's game, but his ankle provided the biggest concern. He will continue to be evaluated throughout the week, but the hope is that he will start Sunday against the Los Angeles Chargers.

"He's good," a source told ESPN. "He'll be fine."

Coach Aaron Glenn declined to comment on the injury earlier Monday but emphasized that Smith remains New York's starter and pushed back on the notion of playing rookie Cade Klubnik for evaluation purposes.

"Geno's our starter," Glenn said on a videoconference with reporters. "Come on now, let's not do that.

"I think Geno's had a really good year, and it would be disrespectful to him to just [ replace him ] . I think we all understand that. I think we all know that he's our starter."

Smith exited twice in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Buffalo Bills. He missed the first series of the third quarter due to a concussion evaluation, then returned for one series before hurting his ankle later in the quarter while falling backward on a knockdown by blitzing safety Cole Bishop.

The Jets (2-8), losers of five straight, face the Chargers (0-8) on Sunday at SoFi Stadium.

The 36-year-old Smith, whose contract expires at the end of the season, is having a solid year as the Jets' bridge quarterback. He's 19th in Total QBR (53.3), with 12 touchdown passes and three interceptions, but the Jets are only 26th in scoring (19.4 points per game).

Klubnik, a fourth-round pick from Clemson, made his NFL debut Sunday. He threw an interception and was sacked three times while completing 11 of 20 passes for 137 yards.

title: NFL confirms Aidan Hutchinson's tackle of Drake Maye was not a hip drop - NBC Sports
description:
Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson and Patriots quarterback Drake Maye were injured on the same play Sunday.
Hutchinson sacked Maye on third down with 9:28 left in the first quarter.
He ripped Maye down from behind, with his right arm reaching around Maye’s right shoulder pad.
The league said it was not a hip-drop tackle because Hutchinson did not swivel or unweight himself.
Patriots coach Mike Vrabel called Hutchinson’s tackle “just part of the game.” “However it happened, I don’t think it was anything intentional,” he said postgame.
text:
Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson and Patriots quarterback Drake Maye were injured on the same play Sunday. Hutchinson sacked Maye on third down with 9:28 left in the first quarter.

He ripped Maye down from behind, with his right arm reaching around Maye’s right shoulder pad. Hutchinson landed on Maye’s lower leg, injuring the quarterback’s ankle. Hutchinson seriously injured his right knee in the celebration.

Fox rules analyst Mike Pereira said on the broadcast that Hutchinson’s tackle was “not a hip drop.”

“Three things have to happen: You have to unweight yourself, swivel all around the back and land on the back of his leg below the knee,” Pereira said. “This was more of a horse collar-type pulled down from behind. [But] certainly not a horse collar penalty.”

Walt Anderson, the NFL’s officiating rules analyst, confirmed Pereira’s explanation through a league spokesman, via Mike Reiss of ESPN. The league said it was not a hip-drop tackle because Hutchinson did not swivel or unweight himself.

No penalty was called on the field.

Patriots coach Mike Vrabel called Hutchinson’s tackle “just part of the game.”

“However it happened, I don’t think it was anything intentional,” he said postgame.

text:
Aidan Hutchinson’s sack-celebration injury is not the first time the Detroit Lions have seen a defender’s season end thanks to having too much fun after putting the opposing quarterback on the ground.

Hutchinson’s reported torn ACL, which will end his 2026 season pending a second opinion according to ESPN, occurred early in the first quarter of the Lions’ 35-10 victory over the New England Patriots in Munich, Germany. But 12 years earlier, former Lions defensive lineman Stephen Tulloch mimicked Aaron Rodgers’ “discount double check” State Farm spot only to land awkwardly and end his season with a torn ACL.

Players have all kinds of ways of expressing their wins play to play. New York Giants running back Cam Skattebo backflips after he scores (or appears at Fanatics Fest with an injured leg). Hutchinson’s injury was a freak accident – and totally avoidable.

Speaking on “Sunday Night Football,” NBC’s Cris Collinsworth said that he would ban players jumping in jubilation if he were an NFL head coach.

“If you’re celebrating a touchdown, a sack, or whatever, it is against the law to leave your feet. No jumping,” he said. “How many more players are we gonna have to see ... have a major injury, celebrating by jumping and landing the wrong way? It made me sick today watching Aidan Hutchinson hurt himself after a great play.”

Hutchinson’s injury wasn’t the lone ailment suffered on the play; Patriots quarterback Drake Maye exited with an ankle injury that could also keep him out for an extended period. It was Hutchinson’s sixth sack of the year.

A sack ended Hutchinson’s 2024 season when he suffered a broken tibia against the Dallas Cowboys. But that occurred during the play.

Hutchinson is certainly not the first NFL player to suffer a serious injury while celebrating. One famous example – certainly more synonymous with the celebration injuries compared to Tulloch – is Washington quarterback Gus Frerotte giving himself a concussion and sprained neck by head-butting a padded concrete wall after scoring a touchdown in a tie against the New York Giants in 1997. As his Chicago Bears were trailing by 25 points against the Patriots in 2014, Lamarr Houston suffered a torn ACL while celebrating – a few weeks after Tulloch went down.

Hutchinson's celebration, which he's done for years, is based on soccer star Cristiano Ronaldo's patented goal celebration ‒ in which the player sprints towards the corner flag, leaps high, twirls in mid-air, then lands with his feet planted wide and his arms extended. Baltimore Ravens kicker Tyler Loop (and essentially the entire team) did the celebration after Loop's walk-off field goal in Brazil in September.

Arizona Cardinals kicker Bill Gramatica also tore his ACL in 2002 by jumping and landing awkwardly after a successful 42-yard field goal.

"For some reason, people tend to remember me every time something like that happens," Gramatica told ESPN. "This is the most high-profile one I think we've seen. It's going to sting for a while, but it won't define him. He's such an incredible athlete and he's going to come back. He's already playing with a chip on his shoulder, it feels like. So this is just going to add to that.

"I think mine will still be the most famous just because they can pick on me. They made fun of a kicker. I guarantee you no one's going to be making fun of him. ... You want to compare me to him? I'll take it."

FLORHAM PARK, N.J. -- New York Jets quarterback Geno Smith, who underwent imaging tests Monday on his left ankle, avoided a major injury, sources told the NFL Network's Ian Rapoport.

Smith dealt with a variety of injuries during Sunday's game, but his ankle provided the biggest concern. He will continue to be evaluated throughout the week, but the hope is that he will start Sunday against the Los Angeles Chargers.

"He's good," a source told ESPN. "He'll be fine."

Coach Aaron Glenn declined to comment on the injury earlier Monday but emphasized that Smith remains New York's starter and pushed back on the notion of playing rookie Cade Klubnik for evaluation purposes.

"Geno's our starter," Glenn said on a videoconference with reporters. "Come on now, let's not do that.

"I think Geno's had a really good year, and it would be disrespectful to him to just [replace him]. I think we all understand that. I think we all know that he's our starter."

Smith exited twice in Sunday's 31-12 loss to the Buffalo Bills. He missed the first series of the third quarter due to a concussion evaluation, then returned for one series before hurting his ankle later in the quarter while falling backward on a knockdown by blitzing safety Cole Bishop.

The Jets (2-8), losers of five straight, face the Chargers (0-8) on Sunday at SoFi Stadium.

The 36-year-old Smith, whose contract expires at the end of the season, is having a solid year as the Jets' bridge quarterback. He's 19th in Total QBR (53.3), with 12 touchdown passes and three interceptions, but the Jets are only 26th in scoring (19.4 points per game).

Klubnik, a fourth-round pick from Clemson, made his NFL debut Sunday. He threw an interception and was sacked three times while completing 11 of 20 passes for 137 yards.

The Detroit Lions are now down their best defensive player.

Edge rusher Aidan Hutchinson is reportedly out for the season after "what initial tests showed to be a torn ACL in his right knee," according to ESPN/NFL Network's Ian Rapoport. Rapoport also reports there is concern about Hutchinson's meniscus.

Hutchinson hurt his knee celebrating a sack of New England Patriots quarterback Drake Maye in the first quarter of their 35-10 win over the Patriots on Nov. 15, 2026.

He was eventually ruled as out and didn't return to the game.

At the time of his injury, Hutchinson led the Lions with six sacks on the season and has played like one of the NFL's best edge rushers. He signed a four year, $180 million contract extension in 2025 that will keep him in Detroit through 2030.

This isn't the first time Hutchinson will miss significant time with a leg injury, however.

Hutchinson broke his left leg in October 2024 in a game against the Dallas Cowboys, with the Pro Bowl defender missing the final 12 games of the 2024 regular season. The Lions went 11-1 in those 12 games, finishing the regular season with a 15-2 record but losing to the Washington Commanders in the divisional round without Hutchinson (and several other key defenders) on the field.

The Lions pass rush still did well without Hutchinson in the game against the Patriots, recording four sacks (two from rookie Derrick Moore, one from Alim McNeill and another from D.J. Wonnum) as the defense held New England to just one touchdown. Moore will likely get more playing time in Hutchinson's absence.

text:
The most devastating play of the 2026 NFL season unspooled in Munich, Germany when Detroit Lions star Aidan Hutchinson turned the corner and chased down New England Patriots star Drake Maye during the first quarter of a Week 10 showdown. Maye suffered a "significant lower leg" injury on the play. Hutchinson was just fine … until he started his celebration.

Hutchinson ran a few yards and leapt in the air to celebrate his sixth sack of the season. When he came down, he had torn his ACL in his right knee. It's a crushing loss for a Lions team that would be the No. 2 seed in the NFC if the NFL Playoffs started today. This is extremely hard to watch now knowing the aftermath of the play.

In the process, Hutchinson joined a dubious list of football players who have been injured while celebrating, and many of them have had disastrous consequences.

Hutchinson's injury was eerily similar to another torn ACL suffered after sacking a New England Patriots quarterback. Back in 2014, Chicago Bears EDGE rusher Lamarr Houston went down with the same injury after celebrating a sack while his team was already down 25 points in the fourth quarter.

Another infamous moment that came to mind was Bill Gramatica's ACL injury. In 2001, Gramatica was a kicker for the Arizona Cardinals who tore his ACL celebrating a 42-yard field goal against the New York Giants.

This still hurts to watch:

How can we forget Gus Frerotte giving himself a concussion after celebrating a touchdown run by headbutting a padded concrete wall? Yikes.

The Lions had another defensive lineman go down on a very similar play to Hutchinson about 12 years earlier. Stephen Tulloch tried to taunt Aaron Rodgers by mimicking the QB's "discount double check" celebration back in 2014. Trying to copy Rodgers' gimmick cost him a torn ACL.

Hutchinson is clearly the best player on this list. His injury brings to mind Dan Campbell's famous line after Detroit lost in January 2024 following the 2023 season.

"I told those guys, this may have been our only shot," Campbell said.

Since then, the Lions have survived the loss of both coordinators to remain an elite team in the NFC. Now they need to persevere again to overcome the loss of arguably their best defensive player. Hutchinson's injury should be a lesson for future generations so history doesn't repeat itself: play it cool after a big moment. You don't want to be next on this list.

Hutchinson injured his knee on the Lions' first defensive series versus the New England Patriots on Sunday in Munich. After sacking New England's Drake Maye, Detroit's fifth-year star jumped in celebration and landed awkwardly on his right leg. Hutchinson immediately went to the turf. As teammates and players approached, he gestured to the front of his right knee.

Hutchinson reportedly underwent an MRI after Detroit's 35-10 win that showed a torn ACL. Lions head coach Dan Campbell said the defensive end would undergo further testing when the team returned to the U.S. before making an official announcement.

"We'll know more when we get back in the States," head coach Dan Campbell said postgame, via the Detroit News' Nolan Bianchi. "Anytime you lose a player of his caliber, the type of teammate he is, he's a captain of ours, that doesn't make things easy."

Meanwhile, a fan captured video of Hutchinson in a wheelchair at the airport prior to the Lions traveling back to Michigan on Sunday.

Maye sustained an injury to his ankle on the same play and the Patriots fear the QB may have suffered a fracture that would end his season. The third-year star stayed in Germany for additional testing that could determine if he needs surgery, Patriots head coach Mike Vrabel confirmed during a radio interview Monday.

In nine games this season, Hutchinson recorded 6 sacks and 24 total tackles in addition to 1 pass defended and 1 forced fumble.

Hutchinson's torn ACL is the second serious, season-ending injury that he has sustained during his NFL career. During the 2024 season, he suffered a broken fibula and tibia in his left leg during a Week 6 win over the Dallas Cowboys. Hutchinson recovered to play in all 17 games last year, compiling 14.5 sacks.

The Lions' 2022 first-round draft pick (No. 2 overall) out of Michigan, Hutchinson has been named to two Pro Bowls and earned second-team All-Pro honors during his career. He's compiled 49 sacks in 65 games with 200 tackles and 5 interceptions.

title: NFL players need to tone down the excessive celebrations after Aiden Hutchinson injury
description:
NFL players should tone down the celebrations.
On Sunday in Germany, Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson tore his ACL while leaping into the air to celebrate his first-quarter sack of Patriots quarterback Drake Maye.
Hutchinson joins an unnecessarily long list of NFL players who injured themselves while celebrating too hard.
A year later, Hutchinson suffered the Stephen Tulloch injury doing the Stephen Tulloch celebration.
Hutchinson found an additional way to do it — and dramatically changed the outlook for Detroit’s next two seasons and his career.
text:
NFL players should tone down the celebrations.

On Sunday in Germany, Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson tore his ACL while leaping into the air to celebrate his first-quarter sack of Patriots quarterback Drake Maye. Hutchinson’s knee buckled when he landed on the turf.

This page may contain affiliate links to legal sports betting partners. If you sign up or place a wager, FOX News may be compensated. This content was created by a team that works independently from the FOX newsroom.

His season is over. His season next year is in jeopardy. The Detroit Lions’ Super Bowl odds fell from +1600 to +2300 at most sportsbooks.

All because of a celebration.

Hutchinson joins an unnecessarily long list of NFL players who injured themselves while celebrating too hard.

In 2014, fellow Lion Stephen Tulloch mimicked Aaron Rodgers’ "Discount Double Check" belt celebration after sacking him, only to tear his left ACL upon landing.

Other examples include 49ers linebacker Dre Greenlaw, who ruptured his Achilles tendon while celebrating a punt on the sideline during Super Bowl LVIII; Bears defensive end Lamarr Houston, who tore his ACL during a garbage-time sack celebration; and kicker Bill Gramatica, who tore his ACL after getting a little too excited about making a 42-yard field goal.

SOPHIE CUNNINGHAM LAUGHS AT STEPHEN A SMITH'S BELITTLING CLAIM ABOUT WHITE NBA PLAYERS

It’s hard enough to avoid injury with athletic specimens charging at you every play. No need to increase the odds with uncontrolled excitement.

We aren’t asking players to suppress natural human emotion. They don’t need to turn into NPCs. However, they could at least keep their feet on the turf.

A fist pump, a group hug, the sign of the cross, or a bottle of champagne after the game would suffice.

NBC color commentator Cris Collinsworth suggested a reasonable team rule while reacting to Hutchinson’s injury later in the day.

"If you're celebrating... It is against the law to leave your feet. No jumping...," Collinsworth proposed.

Indeed.

DIANNA RUSSINI'S CRINGE PODCAST DEBUT RAISES QUESTIONS ABOUT THE VIABILITY OF HER COMEBACK

Players need not perform choreographed routines after every play.

Lions fans were particularly frustrated by Hutchinson’s celebration because, just two weeks earlier, multiple players drew unsportsmanlike conduct penalties for excessive celebration/taunting in a key divisional matchup against the Minnesota Vikings.

Those displays followed standard first-down catches and runs.

Perhaps we could add a provision to Collinsworth’s proposal: save the elaborate celebrations for touchdowns, turnovers, and wins.

Moving the chains does not require an encore. Defensive stops, punts, and pressures don't warrant accompanying theatrics.

If you think that's too harsh, understand this: the Lions would still have their All-Pro defensive end, PFF’s highest-rated defensive player this season, had Hutchinson followed that advice.

A successful NFL career requires proper judgment. Don’t hit opponents after the whistle. Don’t commit needless penalties. Don’t get in trouble off the field.

And don’t put your season, and your team’s, at risk over how you land after celebrating a play.

What's more, Lions fans have long worried about Hutchinson's post-play antics. Social media posts resurfaced Sunday, showing that Lions fans had worried about his airborne routines for years.

"Dear God. Hutch has to stop with the Stephen Tulloch celebration. I hold my breath each time he jumps up and lands," a user named Kory Woods posted in 2025.

A year later, Hutchinson suffered the Stephen Tulloch injury doing the Stephen Tulloch celebration. The phrase déjà vu haunts the Lions in more than one way.

CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP

Bobby, you can get hurt getting out of bed in the morning!

That’s hardly an argument for finding additional ways to do it.

Hutchinson found an additional way to do it — and dramatically changed the outlook for Detroit’s next two seasons and his career.

text:
The outlook for the New England Patriots' 2026 season has been dramatically altered. After suffering an injury on the Patriots' first drive against the Detroit Lions on Sunday, quarterback Drake Maye did not fly back from Munich with the team out of caution, as the team is concerned he might have sustained a fractured ankle.

The 5-5 Patriots haven't been among the AFC's elite in 2026, but were hoping to make a charge to the playoffs -- and Maye potentially finding his past runner-up MVP form was one of their silver linings.

When Maye was taking care of the football and extending plays, the Patriots were explosive and flashed potential to hang with the best -- as a Week 4 win at the Buffalo Bills showed. But when Maye was not buttoned-up with his decision-making (he entered Sunday with 11 INTs), the Patriots struggled to get by some of the league's lower-echelon teams, with close wins against the New York Jets and Miami Dolphins, who have won a combined three games this season.

Coach Mike Vrabel often says it's hard to win when a team's best players don't play well, and simply put, Maye is the team's best offensive player.

Entering Week 10, he ranked top five in the NFL in Total QBR (74.2), passing touchdowns (18), yards per attempt (8.4), rushing yards by a quarterback (219) and rushing touchdowns by a quarterback (3).

Now potentially without Maye for weeks or even the season, the question is can the team make it back to the playoffs?

ESPN Patriots reporter Mike Reiss answers some of the top questions about the trickle-down effect of Maye's injury and analyst Matt Bowen answers a fantasy question on what to expect if you have Patriots players in your lineup.

Is the Patriots' 2026 season over?

When Vrabel was hired as head coach in January 2025, he said the team's goals were to win the division, host home playoff games and compete for championships. Their odds of doing that without Maye are closer to zero, starting with the current standings -- they are 5-5 while the AFC East rival Bills are 8-1.

Here is the rest of the Patriots' schedule: they are on the bye in Week 11 before a road trip to face the winless Los Angeles Chargers, then two huge home games in a span of five days -- vs. the Bills (Dec. 6) and the Minnesota Vikings (Dec. 10). Then they're at the Kansas City Chiefs and the New York Jets before finishing the year with home games against the Denver Broncos and the Miami Dolphins.

They have played poorly the past two weeks in blowout losses to the Packers and Lions, ravaged by injuries across the roster, but Maye's presence -- even as he battled through inconsistent play with turnovers -- gave them a sliver of hope.

Consider what happened Sunday: After New England's opening drive when Maye was injured on the final play, the Patriots totaled seven points and gained 82 yards over 10 drives, averaging 1.9 yards per play (not including kneel down). New England punted on eight of those drives, with seven three-and-outs.

Maye has been the driving force behind the passing game. Entering Sunday, Patriots pass catchers recorded 38.1% of their yards after the catch, the third-lowest total in the NFL behind the Texans (37.1%) and Giants (36.8%), per ESPN Research.

The defense has also mightily struggled as of late, giving the offense little room for error. Since Week 7, the Patriots are giving up the second-most yards per game (411.5), behind only the 1-8 Tennessee Titans.

With some of the NFL's elite teams on the horizon, life without Maye could look bleak.

What is Drake Maye's possible recovery timeline?

The recovery timeline for similar injuries have varied, depending on the severity.

In January, Broncos QB Bo Nix suffered a broken ankle and underwent surgery two days later. The initial recovery timetable reported was 12 weeks. In April, he underwent a clean-up surgery to fix bone spurs. Nix, who had a history of ankle injuries, was ready for training camp in July.

In September 2022, 49ers QB Trey Lance underwent surgery on his right ankle after suffering "a fibula fracture and ligament disruption" in a game. The injury ended his season and required a follow-up surgery in December of that year to remove hardware that was causing irritation. He was cleared to participate in OTAs the following April.

In 2024, 49ers linebacker Fred Warner said he had been playing most of the season with a fractured bone in his ankle.

As we learn more about the specific type of ankle injury Maye has, the timeline will become clearer.

What can the offense get out of Tommy DeVito?

Offensive coordinator Josh McDaniels has been through this before, most recently in 2016 when Tom Brady was serving a four-game NFL suspension and Jimmy Garoppolo and Jacoby Brissett stepped in to help the team to a 3-1 record. McDaniels' offense has flexibility to play to the specific strengths of the quarterback, with an obvious example coming with some designed runs for Brissett in '16 that never would have been called with Brady.

DeVito struggled Sunday when taking over for Maye, and Vrabel noted it was a tough position for him to be thrust into because backups don't receive many, if any, first-team repetitions during the week of practice.

"There were some things that he missed, but also not having a ton of live action since training camp, and really, I think he'll be ready to go coming out of the bye," Vrabel said. "I think that he'll be able to look at some things and understand, whether that's being able to transfer up into the pocket, get us in the right play, get the ball out quicker or look at protections or rotation, whatever that may be. I think that'll all improve."

DeVito had success with the deep ball in the preseason, and made improvements processing information on defensive coverages, so some of the things he has going for him are similar to Maye. And, of course, DeVito briefly caught fire with the New York Giants when thrust into a similar situation.

In eight career starts (all with the Giants), DeVito is 3-5 with a 26.4 QBR, 65.3% completion rate, 1,170 passing yards for 7 touchdowns, one interception and 34 sacks. He isn't as mobile as Maye, with only 36 rushes for 198 yards during those starts.

Vrabel reflected optimism in the backup QB they signed to two-year contract with a maximum value of $7.4 million in March.

"I have a lot of confidence in Tommy," Vrabel said Monday. "I know his toughness is going to be through the charts, and his competitiveness will be exactly what we need."

Could the Patriots explore other options at quarterback?

That is a longer-shot scenario in terms of signing someone to be the starter, mainly due to the intricacies of the offense and the time crunch. A more likely option initially is to utilize the 17-player practice squad to add a third layer of quarterback depth behind DeVito and rookie Behren Morton, the seventh-round pick from Texas Tech.

Another avenue to explore would be other teams' practice squads to see if there was a worthy option to sign to the 53-man roster in a backup role. There are 15 quarterbacks on practice squads, a group including Will Levis (Jets), Nick Mullens (Jaguars), Kyle Trask (Cowboys) Hendon Hooker (Titans), Jake Browning (Chargers) and Luke Altmyer (Lions).

"I don't see that being the case right now, but we'll have conversations and we'll discuss it and we'll look and see," Vrabel said Monday about the possibility of adding a quarterback.

How have injuries decimated the Patriots this season?

New England mostly had good fortune health-wise in its surprise run to the Super Bowl last year, and 2026 has been the other side of the coin. Vrabel noted in a Monday radio interview that it evens out over time.

It began in the spring when tight end Julian Hill, who they signed to be their No. 2 option and a blocking force, sustained a season-ending knee injury and veteran outside linebacker Harold Landry III had an undisclosed injury that landed him on the physically unable to perform list (where he remains). Then receiver A.J. Brown suffered a right high-ankle sprain in the season opener and hasn't looked the same since a strong training camp. They placed both starting guards on injured reserve, along with No. 2 receiver Romeo Doubs (shoulder) and No. 2 running back TreVeyon Henderson (illness), among others. And now possibly Maye.

Teams are allowed eight designations to return from IR and the Patriots have already used five of them and will likely max out all eight by season's end.

"We just have to find some consistency, hopefully, in the lineup with the guys that are coming in and out and everything else, guys that we've built up through the draft and the guys that know one system. But that sometimes always isn't going to be the case, and that's where we're at now," Vrabel said.

What should fantasy managers do with the Patriots' offense in fantasy football?

This injury will have a major impact on the Patriots' roster from a fantasy perspective. DeVito can provide some upside as a runner but he should only be played in deeper Superflex formats as a QB2.

WR A.J. Brown left Sunday's game with a hamstring injury, and he's played in only four games this season due to multiple injuries. When he returns, however, Brown's value declines, fitting in lineups as a WR3. DeMario Douglas now becomes a matchup-dependent WR3, while Mack Hollins is a bye week fill-in for deeper leagues. TE Hunter Henry was a top target for Maye, but I am anticipating a reduced amount of red-zone work here, which moves him down to the TE1/TE2 line.

text:
The Detroit defense is now down its top two players.

Aidan Hutchinson was seen in a wheelchair being carted out of Munich, Germany, Airport where the Lions destroyed the Patriots 35-10.

Fans were seen greeting the star pass rusher as his leg was in an air cast.

Hutchinson sacked Drake Maye in what appeared to be a hip-drop tackle, landing on Maye’s ankle. Maye reportedly suffered a fractured ankle that will end the star Patriots quarterback’s season.

Hutchinson got up and celebrated by jumping, landing awkwardly on his right leg, and then came crashing down to the grass at Allianz Arena.

The Lions’ superstar pass rusher is feared to have torn his ACL during the celebration, which would end his season and could take away part of next year as well.

Detroit has not confirmed the severity of the injury, but he is expected to miss the rest of the season.

The Lions’ defense is already depleted, as they are still reeling from the loss of linebacker Jack Campbell, who suffered from a neck injury that has him in a long recovery, including regaining mobility in his upper body.

With both players likely out for the season, the Lions defense, already rated No. 25 in FTN’s DVOA, will only get worse as they try to win shootouts each week.

The Lions do have a top-10 offense and are No. 5 overall in yards per play (6.0), behind only the 49ers, Chiefs, Bengals and Bills.

Hutchinson has six sacks this season, one forced fumble and is a perennial favorite for Defensive Player of the Year.

Coach Dan Campbell refused to confirm anything related to the severity of the injury after the game.

“Nothing new,” Campbell said postgame. “We’ll know more when we get back in the States. But anytime you lose a player of his caliber, the type of teammate he is, he’s a captain of ours, that doesn’t make things easy.”

Maye, whom Hutchinson tackled on the play, is also expected to miss the rest of the season with a fractured ankle.

The Lions, 7-2, face the Buccaneers at home next Sunday and are currently tied for first in the NFC North.

text:
After sitting out Sunday's win over the Atlanta Falcons while recovering from a groin injury, Kansas City Chiefs star running back Kenneth Walker III reportedly won't miss much more time.

During an appearance on Monday's episode of The Pat McAfee Show, ESPN's Adam Schefter reported that the Chiefs' "idea was to shut [Walker] down for a week" because they "believe that it's a short-term injury."

Even without Walker, the Chiefs cruised to a 35-13 victory over the Falcons. Rookie running back Emmett Johnson racked up a career-high 101 yards on 22 carries while adding six receptions for 70 yards and two touchdowns. Star quarterback Patrick Mahomes was in top form, throwing for 348 yards, five touchdowns and no interceptions.

After sitting out on Sunday, Walker still ranks fourth in the NFL with 872 rushing yards. After signing with Kansas City in free agency over the offseason, he's provided a different dimension to an offense that has long relied on Mahomes' heroics.

Still, Schefter made it clear that the Chiefs will be cautious with Walker's recovery, especially after Johnson's impressive performance. Walker has a history of soft-tissue injuries, and Kansas City will want him healthy for the playoffs.

"There's really not a rush to bring him back when Emmett Johnson is playing the way he is," Schefter said. "So, would it surprise me if it went beyond this week? No. They'll have to see how he's feeling. They did not consider it to be a long-term type of issue when he hurt his groin in practice on Thursday."

In Week 11, the Chiefs will be facing an Arizona Cardinals team that ranks 28th in the NFL with 129.9 rushing yards allowed per game, so they could afford to let Walker rest for another week while Johnson takes the reins if needed.

Initial tests on Aidan Hutchinson’s injured knee showed the Detroit Lions star has a torn ACL, according to a report from NFL Network on Monday, Nov. 16.

Hutchinson, 26, had initial tests performed in Germany, where the Lions beat the New England Patriots on Sunday, and will have more done in the United States, the report added.

On Good Morning Football, NFL Network’s Ian Rapoport said, “my understanding, the belief is it’s a torn ACL and more for Aidan Hutchinson.”

The injury to Hutchinson occurred in the first quarter of Detroit’s win over the Patriots. Hutchinson sacked quarterback Drake Maye and leapt into the air to celebrate. He fell to the ground after landing and grabbed his right knee.

Hutchinson, who has six sacks this season, eventually walked off the field under his own power. He entered the blue medical tent on the sideline and remained there for a few moments before later walking to the locker room with trainers at his side.

"Nothing new," Lions coach Dan Campbell said after the game when asked for an update on Hutchinson. "We’ll know more when we get back to the States. But any time you lose a player of his caliber, the type of teammate he is — he’s a captain of ours — that doesn’t make things easy. But I thought guys stepped up in his wake and showed up for us today and helped us out."

Campbell is scheduled to hold a news conference on Tuesday.

If the report from NFL Network is correct and Hutchinson does have a torn ACL, D.J. Wonnum and rookie Derrick Moore would be expected to see an uptick in responsibilities. Wonnum has six sacks this season, and Moore has four over his last two games.

text:
It was a rough week for the New England Patriots over in Germany. As we look over the Week 11 NFL injury report, the Patriots are going to pop up quite a bit going into their bye. We also have five other teams on bye — the Packers, Seahawks, Browns, Falcons and Rams. Those teams will hopefully get healthier over that span.

Below, we'll go over the latest injury news, providing updates on key players for fantasy football.

Quarterback

Drake Maye, NE (ankle) — Out indefinitely

Geno Smith, NYJ (concussion/ankle)

Sam Darnold, SEA (quad) — bye week

Baker Mayfield, TB (lower leg) — Could miss Week 11

Maye: New England heads into its bye, though the season may be lost coming out of it. At this point, it's feared Maye has a fractured ankle and could need season-ending surgery. At the very least, he could miss multiple games or be placed on IR. It's almost helpful that New England is on bye in Week 11, as fantasy managers would already be looking for a Maye replacement or streaming option.

If Maye is done for the season, it's difficult to trust anyone on this offense. There are injuries and ailments everywhere, from A.J. Brown to Rhamondre Stevenson and TreVeyon Henderson. The Pats are well behind the 8-1 Bills in the AFC East, though are still in the wild-card picture. But if Maye is out, that outlook could change fast. If you have any skill position player on New England, be sure to have contingency plans. This team could turn into a fantasy wasteland soon.

Mayfield: The Bucs are coming out of the Week 10 bye but may be without Mayfield. He suffered a lower leg injury in Week 9's loss to Chicago, and the extra rest didn't appear to help. If Mayfield is out against Detroit in Week 11, Jalon Daniels, who started three games earlier in the season, would get another shot. With so many teams on bye and Maye managers searching for answers, Daniels isn't a bad waiver add. Tampa Bay has a pretty soft schedule the rest of the season. Expect the Bucs to continue to ride the running game with Bucky Irving and Kenny Gainwell.

Running Back

Kenneth Walker III, KC (groin)

Woody Marks, HOU (concussion)

David Montgomery, HOU (groin)

Kyle Monangai, CHI (thumb/toe)

Walker: The Chiefs added Walker to the injury report last Friday and he was swiftly ruled out for Week 10 against the Falcons. As a result, rookie Emmett Johnson thrived in lead-back duties, totaling 171 yards on 28 touches (six catches) with two TDs for 32.1 fantasy points. Reports suggest this will be a short absence for Walker and he should be back Week 11 against the Cardinals.

If Walker is back, he should return to his role as the lead back and get the majority of the work. Johnson has played well enough to warrant touches, however, and could get extra work given the opponent. Kansas City is a heavy favorite in Week 11, and if the team pulls away, we could see Walker rest and Johnson get work in garbage time. If Walker is active, you're playing him, of course. But if you were able to snag Johnson off the wire, he's also in play as a flex option.

Texans RBs: Marks was forced to leave Week 10 against the Browns due to a concussion. He's unlikely to go Thursday against the Colts. Head coach DeMeco Ryans also doesn't know if Montgomery will be ready on the short week. If both backs are out, it's looking like Emari Demercado and Dare Ogunbowale will split the work out of the backfield.

While it's a good matchup, if both Marks and Monty are out, neither depth back is a strong fantasy play. Each would be a risky flex option. Instead, expect the Texans to lean on the passing game, which has looked good over the past four games. Xavier Hutchinson, Tank Dell and Kayshon Boutte remain interesting adds off the waiver wire depending on league size/format.

Wide Receiver

Luther Burden III, CHI (concussion)

Mike Evans, SF (Achilles)

Carnell Tate, TEN (shoulder)

Ladd McConkey, LAC (back)

DeVonta Smith, PHI (hamstring)

A.J. Brown, NE (hamstring) — bye week

Omar Cooper Jr., NYJ (ankle)

Jordan Addison, MIN (thumb)

Wan'Dale Robinson, TEN (ankle)

Marvin Harrison Jr., HOU (hamstring)

Burden: The Bears were on bye in Week 10 and Burden has had ample time to get right. We'll see what his practice status looks like but he'll need to clear protocol in order to play this week against the Saints. If Burden misses the game, it's a bump up for Rome Odunze and Colston Loveland in the pass game, while we may see more targets for Kalif Raymond.

Evans: The Niners may not be in a rush to get Evans back given the 46 points the offense scored on Sunday against the Cowboys. The veteran wideout missed his third straight game but will have a shot at returning in Week 11 against the Vikings, not an ideal spot. San Francisco also has a pretty crowded receiving room with Deebo Samuel Sr. returning and Keenan Allen coming over via trade, not to mention George Kittle and the emerging Jordan Watkins. If Evans can get back in Week 11, he's a low-upside WR2/3 given the matchup.

Tight End

Brock Bowers, LV (ankle)

Bowers: Reports came out that Bowers avoided a major injury in Week 10's loss to the Seahawks, which is good news. He's considered day-to-day and has a shot to play in Week 11 against the Broncos. The tight end didn't get much time to develop chemistry with new starting QB Fernando Mendoza on Sunday, catching just two passes for 18 yards before exiting. With Mendoza under center, it's a slight downgrade for Bowers, but he's still a locked-in TE1. If Bowers ends up missing the game, Michael Mayer isn't a bad streaming option. The Broncos have been a soft matchup for TEs this season.
